key: When the work is done, and one’s name is becoming distinguished, to withdraw into obscurity is the way of Heaven.
s: The chapter calls withdrawing into obscurity, when the work is done and the name grows distinguished, the way of Heaven; the Heshang Gong commentary, on chapter 9, reads it as warning that one who does not step down after success meets harm, which is Heaven’s constant way, as the sun moves on after noon and the full moon wanes.
src: The Heshang Gong commentary, Laozi Daodejing Heshang Gong zhangju, chapter 9, zh.wikisource (a normalised text), revision 2019760 (2021)

evidence.words: 言人所為，功成事立，名蹟稱遂，不退身避位，則遇於害，此乃天之常道也。譬如日中則移，月滿則虧
evidence.gloss: It says that when what a person does has succeeded, the work accomplished and the name made, if he does not withdraw and leave his post he meets harm: this is Heaven’s constant way. It is like the sun moving on after noon and the moon waning when full.

reason: Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok, ref Tao Te Ching 9, at [8]). The Heshang Gong base line 功成、名遂、身退，天之道 matches the key verse, and its comment says one who does not withdraw after success meets harm, calls this Heaven’s constant way, and gives the noon sun and the full moon; the sentence paraphrases this without drift (‘warning’ answers to the comment’s 言 ... 則遇於害). Plain sense faithful. entry-check ok.
